question: Will the earth last forever?
summary: Deuteronomy 4:40, Psalm 37:29, Psalm 78:69, Psalm 104:5, and Ecclesiastes 1:4 all assert that the earth abides forever — Psalm 104:5 specifically says it 'should not be removed for ever.' Psalm 102:25-26, Isaiah 65:17, the Synoptic apocalyptic discourses (Matthew 24:35 and parallels), Hebrews 1:10-11, 2 Peter 3:10-13, and Revelation 21:1 say the earth will perish, melt, pass away, or be replaced by a new earth. The everlasting-earth and perishing-earth traditions are in direct tension.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read the perishing texts as a change of the earth's form, not its annihilation, so the same world that "abides for ever" is renovated rather than destroyed.

discrepancy.connective: Cataloguing this in the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, Steve Wells presses the pairing as a flat contradiction: the texts that say the earth abides for ever and stands "not be removed for ever" cannot both be true alongside those that say it will perish, melt, and pass away.

pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, arguing the heavens and earth 'shall perish... not as to the substance, but as to the quality of them,' so the abiding-earth and perishing-earth texts both stand.

excerpts.excerpt_text: The earth and the heavens in their present state and form "shall perish" … "Perish" does not mean annihilation; just as it did not mean so in the case of "the world that being overflowed with water, perished" under Noah … The covenant of the possession of the earth was renewed with Noah and his seed on the renovated earth. So it shall be after the perishing by fire …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly addresses the core tension: reads the NT 'perish/pass away' language as renovation (change of form), not destruction of substance, so it does not negate the OT 'earth abides for ever' texts.

They--The earth and the heavens in their present state and form "shall perish" (Heb 12:26-27; Pe2 3:13). "Perish" does not mean annihilation; just as it did not mean so in the case of "the world that being overflowed with water, perished" under Noah (Pe2 3:6). The covenant of the possession of the earth was renewed with Noah and his seed on the renovated earth. So it shall be after the perishing by fire (Pe2 3:12-13).
